newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize sales, Colruyt profit seen up.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize sales, Colruyt profit seen up.

text.p: Belgian retail group Delhaize's provisional 1996 results due on Friday should show a turnover increase of around 13 percent thanks to a stronger dollar and good sales at U.S. unit Food Lion, analysts said.
Rival retailer Colruyt is expected to come in with higher profits when it publishes its first half 1996/97 results late on Wednesday afternoon.
Both companies have benefited from an end to Belgium's supermarket price war. But many do not expect the overall sector to shine this year, with little improvement seen in domestic consumption.
Several analysts say Delhaize is their preferred stock among Belgium's biggest retailers, which include GIB Group.
Delhaize shares have been rising since Food Lion, which makes up about two thirds of its consolidated turnover, last week announced its 1996 sales rose 9.7 percent.
"Delhaize remains our favourite Belgian retailer. Our "buy" rating remains unchanged," broker Vermeulen-Raemdonck said in a market research note released after the Food Lion figures.
Delhaize made a group net profit of 3.8 billion Belgian francs and consolidated turnover of 368 billion francs in 1995.
Bank Degroof analyst Jan Longeval said both Delhaize and Colruyt were a "hold" but remained well supported.

He forecast 13 percent sales growth for Delhaize for 1996 and 10 percent in 1997. Though fundamentally overvalued in terms of their dividend discount model, Delhaize shares benefited from a number of factors, he said.
These included Food Lion, dollar strength, the end of GIB's aggressive pricing policy - which led to increased margins - and development in Eastern Europe and Greece where Delhaize has other units.
Food Lion recently bought Florida-based Kash n' Karry, a move considered positive for the long term by analysts.
It is also currently seeking punitive damages from the U.S. ABC television network after already being awarded $1,402 in actual damages by a jury.
Food Lion sued ABC and four producers of its newsmagazine show "Prime Time Live" over a 1992 programme that claimed the grocer sold old food and repackaged out-of-date merchandise.

Sandra Vandersmissen from Generale Bank, who forecast a 12.5 percent increase in Delhaize's consolidated turnover, said the share price would only be impacted by Friday's results if figures for sales in Belgium grew more than expected, say six percent or so.
She calculated a price to expected 1997 earnings ratio of 19 for Delhaize shares, 20 for Colruyt and 19.5 for GIB.

On Colruyt, Generale Bank said in a research note the retailer was expected to show a marked deceleration in first half 1996/97 earnings growth against the previous year. Colruyt's financial year runs to March 31.

The bank forecast a four percent increase in Colruyt's first half net profit to 1.03 billion francs, after a 12.4 percent rise a year earlier, with sales increasing 8.5 percent compared to 12.4 percent in the year-ago period.
The deceleration was largely due to slow sales - particularly of drinks - in the chilly summer months, with consumption generally remaining weak in the other months.
Longeval at Bank Degroof forecast a first half net profit for Colruyt of 1.1 billion francs.
By early afternoon on the Brussels bourse on Wednesday Colruyt shares were 175 francs higher at 14,125 and Delhaize shares 15 francs firmer at 1,950.
-- Lorrayne Smith, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6812, Fax +32 2 230 7710
